Class SerialSocket

java.lang.Object
com.sgware.serialsoc.SerialSocket
All Implemented Interfaces:
Closeable, AutoCloseable
Direct Known Subclasses:
SimpleSerialSocket
public abstract class SerialSocket extends Object implements Closeable
A serial socket ensures its setup, input, and shut down events all run one at a time on the same thread as other sockets created by the same SerialServerSocket even if an exception is thrown.

A serial socket guarantees the following:

  • onConnect() runs first and on the same thread that called SerialServerSocket.run().
  • A separate thread continuously calls read() to read a new message from the socket's input stream as a string. Each time a message is read, receive(String) is called from the thread that called SerialServerSocket.run() with that message.
  • send(String) can be called from any thread to write(String) a message to the socket's output stream.
  • If any SerialSocket methods throw an exception, the exception is reported to onException(Exception) on the same thread that called SerialServerSocket.run(), and the socket will close gracefully.
  • A socket can be closed by the client, by a network problem, because one of its method threw an exception, or by calling close() from any thread. Regardless of how the socket closed, onClose() and then disconnect() are always called in that order on the same thread that called SerialServerSocket.run().
  • onDisconnect() is always called last on the same thread that called SerialServerSocket.run().
Author:
Stephen G. Ware

  • Method Details

    • onConnect

      protected void onConnect() throws Exception
      Always runs first when the socket connects to the server. It runs on the same thread that called SerialServerSocket.run(). If this method throws an exception, this socket will close() and disconnect() without accepting any input.

      By default, this method does nothing. It is meant to be overridden.

      Throws:
      Exception - if a problem occurs

    • read

      protected abstract String read() throws Exception
      Blocks until a new message is received by the socket's input stream. This method does not run on the same thread that called SerialServerSocket.run(). Once this method returns a message, it does not run again until receive(String) has finished processing the message. If this method throws an exception, the socket closes.

      This method is meant to be called only by the socket's listener thread and should not be called from other contexts.

      Returns:
      a newly read message from the socket's input stream
      Throws:
      Exception - if a problem occurs while reading from the socket

    • receive

      protected void receive(String message) throws Exception
      Runs each time the socket reads a new message. This method always runs on the same thread that called SerialServerSocket.run().

      By default, this method does nothing. It is meant to be overridden.

      Parameters:
      message - the message read by the socket's input stream
      Throws:
      Exception - if a problem occurs while processing the message

    • send

      protected void send(String message)
      Sends a message over the socket. This method can be called from any thread. If sending the message causes an exception, the exception will be reported to onException(Exception) from the same thread that called SerialServerSocket.run() (regardless of what thread called this method), and the socket will close.
      Parameters:
      message - the message to send

    • write

      protected abstract void write(String string) throws Exception
      Writes a message to the socket's output stream. This method may be called from any thread.

      This method is meant to be called only by send(String) and should not be called from other contexts.

      Parameters:
      string - the message to write to the socket's output stream
      Throws:
      Exception - if a problem occurs while writing to the socket

    • onException

      protected void onException(Exception exception) throws Exception
      If an exception is thrown at any time by one of the socket's methods, it is reported to this method from the same thread that called SerialServerSocket.run() (regardless of which thread the exception was thrown on).

      By default, this method does nothing. It is meant to be overridden.

      If this method throws an exception, it will be handled by SerialServerSocket.onException(Exception) and the server will shut down. So if this method does nothing, only this socket will shut down when an exception is thrown. However, if this method throws a new exception or re-throws the same exception it was given, it will cause both this socket and the whole server to shut down.

      Parameters:
      exception - the exception that was thrown by one of the server methods
      Throws:
      Exception - if a problem occurs while processing the exception

    • onClose

      protected void onClose() throws Exception
      Runs after the socket is closed, either because a method threw an exception, because the network disconnected the socket, or because close() was called. This method runs on the same thread that called SerialServerSocket.run().

      No new messages will be received after this method runs; however, if this method runs because of a non-network exception or because close() was called, it will still be possible to send(String) messages. If the socket closed because it was disconnected, any messages sent will not be received.

      By default, this method does nothing. It is meant to be overridden.

      Throws:
      Exception - if a problem occurs

    • disconnect

      protected abstract void disconnect() throws Exception
      Disconnects the socket from the network such that it can no longer send or receive new messages. This method should cause read() to stop blocking if it is waiting. This method runs after onClose() on the same thread that called SerialServerSocket.run(). It is possible the socket is already disconnected by the time this method runs if the socket was closed unexpectedly by the network.
      Throws:
      Exception - if a problem occurs while disconnecting the socket

    • onDisconnect

      protected void onDisconnect() throws Exception
      Always runs last just before the socket stops. It runs on the same thread that called SerialServerSocket.run(). By the time this method runs, the socket will have been disconnected, so it is no longer possible to send(String) or receive(String) messages.

      By default, this method does nothing. It is meant to be overridden.

      Throws:
      Exception - if a problem occurs
